summary: Amun-Re is a two-phase auction game where players bid for Egyptian provinces then decide how much of their gold to spend on farming versus sacrificing to Amun-Re for bonus points, with a second round resetting land and forcing new pyramid-building decisions. The tension comes from balancing short-term income against long-term pyramid value, all under a hidden/simultaneous bidding system that punishes overpaying.
praised: Clever push-your-luck bidding mechanism where money becomes worthless if you don't spend it
Tight, tense auctions with meaningful opportunity cost
Good player interaction through competitive bidding without direct conflict
Elegant, well-integrated theme of provinces, farming, and pyramid-building
Quick to teach relative to its depth
criticised: Luck of the province/bonus tile draw can swing available value
Two-round structure can feel like it resets progress just as things get going
Some player elimination-adjacent frustration if you're outbid on key provinces repeatedly
Can suffer from analysis paralysis during bidding for experienced players
win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Points come almost entirely from pyramid stones built each round plus end-game pyramid-size bonuses, driven by how well you managed farming income versus sacrifices
